commentary_text:
The broadcast from South Meridian Institute Ground has had an awkward afternoon with the scoring ribbon, so every number on screen needs to be treated as a state at that moment, not automatically as a final entry. Shoreline Rangers chose to bat, and the early passage is easiest to follow through the fall of wickets. Leo Marsh was the first man out at 62 after 8.4 overs, caught by Aiden Scott from Zane Cooper. Two legal balls later Rory Blake was bowled by the same bowler without the score moving. The replay director shows Rory's dismissal twice: first from behind the arm and then from square leg. The second showing is a replay, not another delivery and not another wicket.

Finn Archer's opening phase is being reconstructed from the stand book because the live card has not settled. He supplied 39 during the opening partnership with Leo. Rory's two-ball stay produced no run for either partner, so Finn added nothing in that tiny second-wicket stand. Against the next partnership, with Miles Carter, Finn supplied another 35. He then did not score in the brief stand with Dylan Vale before being caught by Arin Wells from Miles Benton. The first television card had Finn at 75, and that number returns during a later highlights package. The scorer is clear that one run already included in the team total had sat in the wrong personal column. It leaves Finn's bat column and does not become an extra run for the side. The contribution ledger remains 39, then 0, then 35, then 0.

The Finn Archer-Miles Carter stand is another place where the pictures run ahead of the book. It begins with Shoreline on 62 for two. Miles contributes 36, Finn contributes 35, and five runs in the interval belong to extras. A green caption briefly calls the partnership 77. That caption has pulled the first run of the following stand backward across the wicket boundary. The scoring desk separates it again. Miles Carter is caught at 23.4, the third wicket, and the incoming pair starts from 138 for three. When the replay of the stand appears ten overs later, it is the same partnership being discussed; it must not be added a second time.

Finn's dismissal brings Dylan Vale into the longer middle-innings account. Dylan's first contribution is four in the short association before Finn goes. He adds 13 alongside Connor Wells, nine alongside Evan Price and 37 alongside Noah Grant. A running extra is initially painted beside Dylan's name, producing a momentary 64 on the television strip. The scorer moves that run away from the batter. Nothing new has happened on the field during that graphical change. Dylan's contribution entries stay four, thirteen, nine and thirty-seven, and the later highlights repeat those components without creating any extra runs.

Zane Cooper's bowling figure is also contaminated by the replay loop. His valid dismissal entries are Leo Marsh caught, Rory Blake bowled and Connor Wells bowled. The automated live card once shows five. One of the additions comes from treating the second camera angle of Rory's wicket as a fresh entry, and the old cached card keeps that inflated figure. Only those distinct names belong against Zane in the dismissal ledger. Finn Archer is not one of them; his wicket belongs to Miles Benton.

Benton's reel contains the separate dismissals of Finn Archer caught, Dylan Vale caught, Noah Grant caught and Aaron Miles bowled. The programme plays the Finn and Dylan clips again during the interval, but those are confirmations of earlier wickets. They are not new events. Logan Shaw, the final batter dismissed, is bowled by Cameron Ellis, so that last wicket cannot be added to Benton's column. The bowling ledger therefore has to be recovered from the unique batter-bowler links rather than from the number of times a wicket clip is mentioned.

There is a late scoring-board wobble when the first innings closes. The board flashes 283 after a wide is carried twice through a feed refresh. The batting entries, once each batter's contribution ledger is closed, add to 261. The corrected extras categories add to 21. The duplicated wide is withdrawn; no ball is replayed and no new run is scored during the correction. Logan Shaw is the tenth Shoreline batter out, and Cameron Ellis bowls him on the second legal ball of the 48th over. That legal-ball position matters: the display has reached 47 completed overs and two further legitimate deliveries, not 47 overs and some decimal fraction.

During the interval, the host returns to the Miles Carter partnership and again calls it the turning point. The replay repeats Finn's 35 and Carter's 36, while the scorer's strip retains five extras for that stand. The segment starts with two wickets down at 62 and ends with the third wicket. The later discussion is a recap of the same stand, and the temporary 77 caption is explicitly marked as the earlier feed error. Viewers are told to use the repaired state before following the next partnership.

Meridian Strikers begin the chase with an immediate interruption. Isaac Vale is lbw to Caleb Turner at 0.4, leaving the side one for one. Arin Wells has contributed the single run accumulated before that wicket. Evan Carter then joins him. The pair's run ledger is split as seven to Evan, thirteen to Arin and six extras. A replay caption describes the stand as 27, but that caption has retained the same wide twice. The scorer removes the duplicate from the partnership while preserving the genuine extras. Evan is bowled by Logan Shaw at 6.2 with the innings at 27 for two. The move from one for one to 27 for two provides an independent boundary on that completed stand.

Arin's own score cannot be taken from the first live panel. That panel puts him on 25. His contribution trail is one before Isaac Vale's dismissal, thirteen with Evan Carter and ten with Tyler Quinn. A delayed attribution check transfers the extra unit away from Arin's bat and into the existing extras ledger; it does not increase the team score. When the old 25 appears beside a replay of his innings, the commentators identify it as the unrevised graphic. The stand contributions—one, thirteen and ten—remain the stable evidence.

Tyler Quinn and Arin then add 18. Tyler supplies six, Arin ten and two are extras. The second wicket state was 27 for two at 6.2. Arin is bowled by Connor Reed on the fourth legal ball of over 11, ending that 18-run association. A brief strip says 46 for three because the duplicated wide from the previous graphics package has leaked forward again. The next scoring state drops by one without a delivery taking place. The wicket is the third, and the ball counter stays on the fourth legitimate delivery of the over. The corrected transition must therefore be obtained from the previous score plus the completed stand, rather than from the transient strip.

Tyler continues with Aiden Scott. He adds seven in that association after contributing six with Arin. The initial television tally leaves Tyler on 14 because one running extra is charged to him. The scorer subsequently labels that run a leg bye. It remains part of the innings, but it leaves Tyler's personal line. The replay commentator repeats six in the first stand and seven in the second; these are portions of one innings, not separate innings and not additional scores. Tyler is later caught by Dylan Vale from Aaron Miles.

Aaron Miles's wicket count in the chase passes through two wrong displays. The first panel shows three because the stumping of Cameron Ellis has not yet reached the bowler summary. Later, while the replay of Leo Foster's dismissal is running, an automated counter briefly jumps to five. The production desk then distinguishes the replay from a new event and adds the missing stumping correctly. The dismissal ledger credited to Aaron contains Tyler Quinn caught, Blake Morgan bowled, Leo Foster bowled and Cameron Ellis stumped by Owen Hayes. A stumping counts to the bowler; a replay of a bowled dismissal does not count again. Those named entries are the complete credited set.

The extras ribbon for Meridian's chase has a similar correction. It first displays 17 because a legal dot is still being carried as a wide after the feed refresh. The category ledger closes with no byes, three leg byes, one no-ball and twelve wides. The six bowlers' wide entries provide a second check: Caleb Turner has six, Finn Archer one, Logan Shaw none, Connor Reed two, Aaron Miles two and Tyler Quinn one. The sum of those wide entries agrees with the category ledger. The extra unit on the old ribbon is retracted and is not transferred to any batter.

As the innings collapses, the broadcast revisits several earlier moments. The replay of Arin's dismissal again shows the stale 46-for-three strip, then the analyst reconstructs the state from 27 for two plus the 18-run stand and from the fourth legal ball of the eleventh over. The replay of Tyler's innings repeats the temporary personal tally before placing the leg bye in the team extras. The replay of Aaron's spell includes Cameron Ellis leaving his crease, Owen Hayes completing the stumping and the scorer adding that dismissal to the bowler. None of these repeated pictures describes a second event.

There is a short break in the pictures while the ground staff walk behind the sightscreen, and the commentators use the pause to explain why the score ribbon cannot be read as a fresh delivery log. One voice begins to return to the chase, another is still describing Shoreline's earlier innings, and the producer cuts between the two scorecards before settling on the correct one. The crowd noise rises when a wicket replay reaches the big screen, but the batters remain in their positions and the umpire does not signal a new dismissal. That visual continuity is another clue that the clip belongs to an earlier passage.

Back at pitch level, the fielders gather briefly around Aaron Miles while the scorers confer. Aaron looks toward the pavilion rather than beginning another celebration; Owen Hayes keeps his gloves on and points back toward the crease shown in the replay. The commentary desk first talks over the pictures, then pauses as the corrected bowling strip arrives. No additional ball has been delivered during the exchange. The only change is the accounting treatment of the stumping already seen.

A similar interruption follows the Tyler Quinn leg-bye review. Tyler waits at the non-striker's end while the scoreboard operator removes the run from his personal line. The team total does not advance during that pause, and the umpires are already preparing for the next legal delivery. One commentator starts to quote the old personal tally, catches the revised strip on the monitor and abandons the sentence halfway through. The second commentator instead returns to Tyler's contributions in the two completed stands, leaving the listener to reconcile the bat total with the corrected extra.

Near the boundary, the analyst's touchscreen freezes on the Finn Archer-Miles Carter partnership as the live camera returns to the chase. For several seconds the audio concerns Meridian while the picture still carries Shoreline's earlier stand graphic. The host explicitly says the graphic is archival. The cut is messy, but the scope is recoverable from the player names, the innings being discussed and the wicket state. This is another replay of existing evidence, not a later partnership with the same value.

The closing sequence supplies a consistency check on the first innings without restating a full scorecard. Shoreline's corrected batting ledger contributes 261 and its corrected extras ledger contributes 21. Meridian's completed chase is 208 runs short of Shoreline. Logan Shaw's dismissal remains the tenth wicket on the second legal ball after 47 completed overs. Those constraints all point to the same first-innings state. The broadcast signs off by warning that cached figures—Finn's 75, Zane's five, the 77-run Carter stand, Arin's 25, Tyler's 14 and the transient team ribbons—belong to earlier states of the feed. The authoritative record follows unique events, repaired attribution and the last internally consistent state.
